about: Question design v3 for the Assignment 02 pilot (ECE 2514): the case design. Every student gets the same LOGIC main question per function (correct = the spec answer, from the reference). What happens next depends on two things: whether the logic answer is right, and whether the student's own code is right for that function (codeRight: it gives the spec answer on every safe candidate input of the import record). Case 1 = logic right, code right; case 2 = logic right, code wrong; case 3 = logic wrong, code right; case 4 = logic wrong, code wrong. Up to 2 follow-ups per function, all about the student's code. Fields "spec" and "key" of the main and small questions and "spec"/"refStops" of the inputs are computed by running the reference (compute-keys.js, run-all.js); do not edit them by hand.
placeholders: Case 1 follow-ups: predict = functions[fn].predict.question with {input}; tracing = tracingQuestion with {line} {function} {input} {kth} {what}; what-if = caseTemplates.whatIf with {line} {function} {oldLine} {newLine} and functions[fn].whatIfTail with {input}. Case 2: caseTemplates.debug with {function} {output} {input} {spec}. Case 3: functions[fn].case3Question. Case 4: functions[fn].small.question.
tracingQuestion: You put a breakpoint on line {line} and run {function} on {input}. When it stops for the {kth} time, {what}?
compileErrorQuestion: Your {function} doesn't compile. The compiler points to line {line}. What is wrong on that line, and how would you fix it?
compileErrorOutsideQuestion: Your code doesn't compile. The compiler points to line {line}. What is wrong on that line, and how would you fix it?
backup: mode is the backup. It replaces a function ONLY when that function is completely missing (no definition) and takes its place: its logic question, its case follow-ups, and (case 1) the type of the follow-up of the function it replaces.
inputRules: An input where the code crashes, gives a runtime error or hits the time limit is never used (undefined behavior). The next separating input is used; if none, a standard input with targeted = false.

playCraps inputs whose answer depends on the validation reading in SPEC-NOTES.md (an invalid value after the game is already decided) have unclearSpec = true and are not used until the spec is confirmed.
Inputs that end with a delimiter, and playCraps inputs with an odd number of values, are never used (not defined by the spec).

rotation.note: The type of follow-up 1 in case 1. Students are sorted by importId and alternate A, B, A, B. mode takes the type of the function it replaces.

clarify: Can you give the exact result?

caseTemplates.debug: Your {function} returns {output} for {input}. Why does it give that instead of {spec}?
caseTemplates.change: Which line would you change, and how?
caseTemplates.whatIf: Suppose line {line} of your {function} were changed from `{oldLine}` to `{newLine}`. With that change, {tail}
caseTemplates.note: Outside case 2 no follow-up states the correct answer, the spec answer or the code's output. Case 2 is the only case that shows their output and the spec answer. Follow-up 2 of cases 3 and 4 is a smaller code step written by the agent (M5b) from the private material in the plan.

about_compile: A function that exists but does not compile gets a compile-error question instead of its logic question (no follow-ups). An error outside the functions replaces the first function's question. When nothing compiles the first function gets the compile-error question and the other two keep their logic main questions with no follow-ups.
